subject: Horizon Health - evidence pack and no-train commitment
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com, legal@horizonhealth.com
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial ask: no-train commitment + evidence for procurement

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams are asking for two things before we move to an internal procurement review: a contractual "no-training / no-derivatives" commitment for the model endpoints we'll use, and a set of artifacts that show how Redwood enforces that in practice (proofs of data handling, subprocessor inventory, and an export path for tenant data).

Can you confirm what you can commit to in the DPA (no training on customer content) and share an evidence pack we can attach to our procurement request? We also need a short checklist that our security team can follow to verify the claim.

Timebox: we'd like to get something by Friday so it can go into the review next week.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Menon
Director, Vendor Ops | Horizon Health
rajiv@horizonhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Initial ask: no-train commitment + evidence for procurement

Hi Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can provide a contractual no-training commitment scoped to the endpoints you configure (we call this a "no-learn" configuration in the DPA), plus an evidence pack that outlines operational controls and export paths.

What we'll include in the pack (summary):
- Signed DPA amendment language for no-training on customer-provided data (scoped to selected models/routes).
- Subprocessor inventory snapshot and attestations.
- Operational playbook: how requests are routed, how KV/prefix caching is scoped, and how we configure dedicated no-learn runtime options.
- Proof artifacts: audit log extracts showing disabled learning flags, export instructions (SFTP/API) and sample deletion attestations.

Dev, looping you in for: 1) a zipped evidence bundle we can send, 2) an ops-level checklist Rajiv's security team can run, and 3) a simple one-page blurb legal can attach to the procurement packet.

Rajiv — we'll target an initial bundle by Thursday EOD to hit your Friday review. If procurement needs a specific format (CSV manifest, signed PDF), flag it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial ask: no-train commitment + evidence for procurement

Hey all —

I've packaged the technical artifacts Rajiv requested and attached them to this thread (redwood_no_train_evidence.zip). Contents at a glance:
- subprocessor_inventory_2025-10.csv (columns: name, country, purpose, access_level, contract_signed)
- audit_extract_no_learn.jsonl (sample entries showing learning_flag=false for tenant_id=hh-001)
- sftp-instructions.pdf (how Horizon Health can pull tenant exports; includes rotation/keys guidance)
- deletion_attestation_sample.pdf (template of the attestation we provide after requested deletion)

Notes/clarifications:
- The DPA amendment we propose is limited to the tenant(s) you specify and to the model endpoints we serve. It prevents training/weight updates and any persistent fine-tuning using your supplied content. It does not prevent Redwood from using aggregated anonymized telemetry for internal performance monitoring (we can carve that out if you need stricter language).
- For cryptographic separation we use customer-managed KMS in private deployments; hosted customers get an isolated runtime with logical separation and audit logging.
- Export path: we support SFTP export and a secure API pull; the instructions in the PDF include checksum verification and an example script.

Security checklist (short):
1) Verify subprocessor CSV matches your procurement registry.
2) Request audit extract for a representative date range — we provided sample lines in the JSONL.
3) Run SFTP key exchange and fetch a sample export.
4) Validate deletion attestation after a test object removal.

If you want, we can redact the audit extract further or provide additional timestamps for the example.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@horizonhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 14:00:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Initial ask: no-train commitment + evidence for procurement

Rajiv, Marissa —

I've reviewed the proposed DPA wording and the evidence artifacts Dev attached. High level: legal is comfortable with a scoped no-training commitment as drafted, subject to two small clarifications:

1) Add explicit language defining the "scope of data" (i.e., tenant IDs, buckets, and API routes) to avoid ambiguity.
2) Add an explicit retention minimum for audit logs (we propose 90 days by default; we can extend if you require).

I'm attaching a one-page summary (inline below) that you can drop into procurement: it states the no-train commitment, the runtime/ops controls, and the artifacts included. If Horizon needs signed appendices, we can produce a signed PDF.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

-- one-page summary (for procurement) --
Redwood: No-Training Commitment (summary)
- Commitment: Redwood will not use customer-provided content from specified tenant IDs for model training, fine-tuning, or derivative model creation. Commitment is scoped to the model endpoints and routes specified in the DPA amendment.
- Evidence: subprocessor inventory, audit log extracts, export instructions, deletion attestation templates.
- Verification: Horizon can request export + audit extracts for a 30-day sample period; Redwood will provide within 3 business days.
- Logs retention: default 90 days (extendable by mutual agreement).
